title: Setup: a dealt start, which is the only shape a game begins in
rationale: Every square of the standard array is filled and no other point is; the two generals stand face up on e1 and e10, the only pieces that ever start face up; the other thirty stand face down; each side's fifteen hidden identities are a permutation of that side's fifteen non-general pieces — two chariots, two horses, two elephants, two advisors, two cannons and five soldiers — and neither permutation is the identity one, a soldier standing on a chariot's square and a chariot on an advisor's; and Red moves first. That is the whole of the membership question this game answers in place of a setup-legality predicate, because there is no composed position for one to judge: there is a start for every deal and nothing else is a start at all.
